trust_decision.summary: The AUSF decides whether a UE's authentication response is genuine: the 5G-AKA confirmation handler compares the UE/SEAF-supplied Res* with the stored Xres* by plain case-insensitive string equality, the EAP-AKA' confirmation handler compares AT_MAC with the computed XMAC using bytes.Equal and XRES with RES by Go string equality, and both flows write XRES*/RES* into the log. All of it lives in internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names non-constant-time authentication comparison and XRES* logging in 5G-AKA; the first site a reader greps for is the 'Compare the received RES* with the stored XRES*' comment, the res*/Xres* log line and the strings.EqualFold call directly beneath it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can leave the EAP-AKA' K_aut trace log alone by arguing it is only emitted at trace level (logger.level must be set to trace) and that the advisory, its title and both log removals are about XRES*/RES* in 5G-AKA, not EAP-AKA' key material.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Case-insensitive hex comparison: strings.EqualFold lets a client-supplied Res* in upper or mixed case match the stored lower-case Xres* (hex.EncodeToString output). The fix keeps this by hex-decoding both sides before the constant-time compare. The obvious fix, subtle.ConstantTimeCompare on the raw strings or bytes.Equal on their bytes, silently rejects otherwise valid confirmations whose hex letters differ in case.

O6_input_shapes: hex-encoded string pair (client Res* vs stored Xres*) in any letter case, decoded to bytes before comparing
raw []byte pair for AT_MAC vs the computed 16-byte XMAC
malformed, odd-length or non-hex string input returns false instead of panicking
unequal-length byte inputs are rejected by the length guard before the constant-time compare
